data.text/markdown:
The training data: what the VAE sees

Everything below reads the pipeline artifacts, never the 75 MB CSV:
Artifact Built by Holds
data/interim/objects.parquet make data one row per object: raw flux, absolute sigma, validity mask, metadata
data/interim/band_scales.parquet make data per-band soft scale b_j
data/processed/jpas_asinh.parquet make features the model input x, its uncertainty sigma_x, the mask
data/interim/folds.parquet make splits leave-one-tile-out fold per object
The model is trained on flux and uncertainty only. Labels (zsp, zph, spCLASSsdss, photoCLASSsdss) and position/metadata columns are carried alongside for inference and diagnostics, never fed in.

1. One row per object

load_arrays() returns aligned numpy arrays plus identifiers. Nothing else is needed to start training.
objects 64,293
bands per object 60
array shapes x, sigma_x, mask = (64,293, 60)
objects with all 60 uncertainties measured 60,991
pixels with no measured uncertainty 38,916 (1.01%)
folds 4

How to load it

from jpas_da.features import load_arrays

a = load_arrays()          # -> dict of arrays
x, sigma_x, mask = a["x"], a["sigma_x"], a["mask"]
fold = a["fold"]           # leave-one-tile-out assignment
x and sigma_x are float32 of shape (n_objects, 60), mask is int8. Band order is canonical and identical in all three arrays - it comes from jpas_da.bands.BAND_NAMES, so no column matching is needed and no ordering can drift.

2. The 60 channels

block n members why it is in the tensor
narrow 54 J0378 ... J0910 the J-spectrum: a 10 nm grid (J0378->J0390 is 12 nm), FWHM ~14.5 nm

data.text/markdown:
The transform

x_b     = asinh(f_b / b_b) * 2                     # model input
sigma_x = sigma_f / sqrt(f_b**2 + b_b**2) * 2      # propagated uncertainty
f_b     = b_b * sinh(x_b / 2)                      # exact inverse
quantity source note
f_b flux_<band> in the interim table FLUX_AUTO, zeropoint 26.1147 (these are not uJy)
sigma_f abs(flux * FLUX_RELERR_AUTO) the export's error is signed relative, so it must be multiplied by the flux
b_b b_j per band median sigma_f
2 features.PRESENTATION_SCALE monotonic global factor that only sets the numerical size of the channels and changes no distance ordering
The 2 matters less than it looks: asinh(x)/s is monotonic, so any analysis that standardises, whitens or computes distances is invariant to it. It is kept in the file so the inverse stays exact. check_roundtrip asserts x -> f on every build. Re-running it on the shipped file: over the 3,818,664 measured pixels the maximum relative error is 5.3e-07 (median 3.4e-08), which is the float32 storage limit. A model output therefore maps back to physical flux with no approximation step. Masked pixels are excluded and cannot invert: their x is 0 by construction, which is exactly why they must be excluded from the loss rather than reconstructed.

data.text/html:
5. The uncertainty survives the transform

A heteroscedastic Gaussian likelihood needs sigma in the same coordinate as the data, so the error is propagated by the chain rule, d asinh(f/b)/df = 1/sqrt(f^2 + b^2). That is the property which makes this representation worth the trouble:
  • in flux units the median sigma grows 4.6x across flux deciles;
  • in asinh units it spans only 1.7x over the nine faintest deciles, and the final collapse (6x lower) is real - the brightest objects genuinely are measured better.
So the model does not need a separate "trust bright pixels more" mechanism: the sigma channel already says it.

data.text/markdown:
8. What the 60 numbers actually vary with

Split each spectrum into an overall level and a shape (x - mean(x)):
component share of total variance
per-object brightness (level) 65%
SED shape (colour) 35%
Brightness dominates. It is a distance/luminosity axis, so it carries real physics and is deliberately not normalised away. Two consequences:
  • For the VAE, most latent capacity and most reconstruction loss will go on brightness unless you condition on it or reserve an explicit latent dimension for it.
  • For Gromov-Wasserstein, the distance matrix is brightness-dominated. If the question is about SED families, factor brightness out at the distance step rather than by re-transforming the data - that keeps the stored representation invertible.

## 9. Splits: leave one pointing out

| fold | held-out tile | test objects | train objects |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2241 | 20,016 | 44,277 |
| 1 | 2243 | 13,836 | 50,457 | | 2 | 2406 | 15,792 | 48,501 | | 3 | 2470 | 14,649 | 49,644 | 
Grouping by tile is not cosmetic. Objects are never shared between pointings,
but neighbours *inside* one pointing share sky background and a common
photometric calibration. A random row split would train and score on the same
noise, and would report a number the survey cannot reproduce on a new field.

```python
train, test = np.flatnonzero(fold != k), np.flatnonzero(fold == k)
```

Because the pointings also differ in depth (~0.16 dex), a fold score is
partly a depth-mismatch score. That is the intended reading, not an artefact.

10. Feeding it to the VAE

a = load_arrays()
x, sigma_x, mask = a["x"], a["sigma_x"], a["mask"]
train = a["fold"] != k

# 60 flux channels + 60 mask channels -> 120 inputs
inputs = np.concatenate([x[train], mask[train].astype("float32")], axis=1)

# heteroscedastic Gaussian likelihood, measured pixels only
valid = mask[train] == 1
noise = sigma_x[train] ** 2
loss = ((rec - x[train]) ** 2 / (2 * noise) + np.log(sigma_x[train]))[valid].mean()
The pipeline already guarantees:
requirement where it is enforced
finite inputs, no NaN in x features.build_representation raises otherwise
sigma_x defined exactly where mask == 1 asserted at build time and in tests/test_data.py
canonical band order jpas_da.bands.BAND_NAMES, a single definition
exact invertibility features.check_roundtrip, run on every build
no label leakage labels live in objects.parquet; x holds 60 flux channels and nothing else
no train/test leak folds.parquet, one fold per pointing
Do not feed MAGrSDSS (exactly 26.1147 - 2.5*log10(rSDSS)), angDist (non-null exactly on the SDSS-cross-matched rows), or any of zsp/zph/avg_zph/spCLASSsdss/photoCLASSsdss. All are kept in the interim table for later inference; none belongs in x.
